commenti.body: I loved his OUTIH novelization so maybe I'm the wrong person to ask, but I liked Cinema Speculation a lot. Engaging writing style and interesting historical details and hot takes, plus some fairly moving memoir-adjacent aspects to it. Lot of subtext on what sounds like a lonely and unstable childhood. His Bill Simmons-esque "What ifs" are a little tedious to me ("What if Brian De Palma directed Taxi Driver?" Well, he didn't!), but his passion and knowledge of 60s-70s film are really winning for me.
That’s definitely his “niche era.” I really enjoy Tarantino as a writer and can’t wait to read this; thanks 👍

I have zero interest in the novel, but I loved Cinema Speculation. Tarantino knows the movies he’s discussing inside and out and has been thinking about them for decades, and generally has interesting and unorthodox things to say about them. It’s well-argued idiosyncratic film criticism that I think most cinephiles would appreciate regardless of their feelings on Tarantino (with respect to both his films and his personality). I also listened to the audiobook version, so you get to hear Quentin himself read the opening and closing chapters, which really sing imo.

I am not a huge Tarantino-head, but I enjoyed reading this book. It is definitely a solid piece of film criticism and analysis. Weirdly, I had no real desire to see any of the movies he was talking about, even though I appreciated reading about them. 

The thing I liked the most is that Tarantino really dials into a zeitgeist about movies in the 70's, why certain movies mattered, why certain themes kept coming back, and along the way he really hits the nail on the head vis-a-vis a lot of the racial and cultural tensions of the era, in a way I think a lot of people talking about these movies now have forgotten (or intentionally obscured). Tarantino really places you there in the milieu and contextualizes these films very well.
